source_checks.finding: The page says exactly: 'Change passwords on all your online shopping accounts in case they were compromised.' The alert is about a package the user did not order, so the ref applies.

The page says exactly: 'If the package came from Amazon or another online marketplace, send the platform a message' and 'so they can investigate removing the seller.' The page presents this as a conditional suggestion, not a requirement. The sentence is on the page, but the fetch did not show it under the heading 'Change passwords' that the ref names. This is a label issue for the card only, not a reason to revise.

The 'Don't contact the sender' section says: 'If you search online for the sender and reach out,' and 'anyone who responds will likely try to get more sensitive information from you' 'to steal your money.' The ref excerpt is a fair excerpt of this.

The closing paragraph says: 'Got a package you didn't order? Keep the merchandise and report fake reviews and scams to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.' This is not a headed section as the ref implies, but the words are on the page and the ref applies to any unordered package.

The 'Check your credit' section says: 'Check your credit weekly for free at AnnualCreditReport.com' 'to monitor the information in your credit report and check for signs of identity theft.' The ref applies to any unordered package.

required_actions.action: Change passwords on all online shopping accounts
Do not contact the seller or sender
Report fake reviews and scams to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Check credit weekly for free at AnnualCreditReport.com
Watch for signs of identity theft
Send the marketplace or app a message so it can look into removing the seller, only if the package came from a marketplace (the user does not want to message anyone, so this stays optional)
